newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says Indian missiles threat to security.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says Indian missiles threat to security.

text.p: Pakistan said on Monday after its arch-foe India tested a missile that New Delhi's missile development was a threat to regional security.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman, reacting to India's test-firing of the surface-to-surface short-range Prithvi missile on Sunday, said this weapon "served to exacerbate tensions" and threatened to start a new arms race that Islamabad wished to avoid.
"While Pakistan is seeking to improve relations, India's missile development programme poses an increasing threat to regional security," the spokesman said.
The Prithvi, which has a range of up to 250 km (160 miles) and can carry a one-tonne warhead, has been tested 16 times since 1982 but has yet to become fully operational.
Pakistan sees the Prithvi and other missiles being developed by India as a threat to its security.

The two countries have fought three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir, where India is fighting a separatist revolt in the two thirds of the region it rules. Pakistan controls the remainder of the territory.
